title: Internal compactness of a constructible skeleton in the geometric finite-field setting
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k$ is the chosen algebraic closure of the finite field $k_0$. Let $\ell\ne p$ be prime and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring isomorphic to a finite discrete commutative ring killed by an $\ell$-power, $\mathbf Z_\ell$, a valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, or the finite-subextension-valued condensed algebraic closure. Let $S=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $L=\Loc(S)$ [sk-def-localizing-closure], and let $g:G\to S$ be an isomorphism-class representative family with $G:\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$, surjective on isomorphism classes and skeletal. There exists a fixed-universe coproduct structure on the full category $L$ such that for every choice of membership proofs $h_L(i):L(g(i))$, every object $(g(i),h_L(i))$ is compact in $L$ in the sense of [def-pc-compact-object]. All coefficient isomorphisms are ring-object isomorphisms; the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure is not replaced by the ring of all continuous maps.

source.place: Compactness, and its identification with compactness in the full localizing subcategory

proof.text: Apply the existing ambient canonical Hom-map compactness assertion to this datum, coefficient object, and skeletal representative family.

Obtain fixed-universe coproducts of the full localizing category from the generic structural theorem, and ambient coproducts from the localizing-closure existence theorem. The intersection defining L is closed under coproducts indexed in its object universe. Restrict this closure along the equivalence of a small discrete index type with its universe lift. The full inclusion therefore creates and preserves each required coproduct.

Apply the existing fully faithful compactness comparison from BrownHypothesesGeneration to the inclusion. Its additive Hom equivalences induce a direct-sum equivalence. The target Hom equivalence composes with the canonical coproduct comparison. The resulting square of canonical Hom maps commutes on each summand, so ambient bijectivity gives internal bijectivity. This works for every membership proof by proof irrelevance and includes empty coproduct index types.

theorem brownHypothesesFiniteFieldCompactness
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : ℓ ≠ D.p)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (hΛ :
      (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A)
          (_ : DiscreteTopology A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A),
        Finite A ∧ (∃ r : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ r) • a = 0) ∧
          Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj A))) ∨
      Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ])) ∨
      (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
        Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E))) ∨
      Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℚ_[ℓ])) ∨
      (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
        Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E))) ∨
      Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ)))
    (G : Type (u + 1)) (g : G → ConstantModelConstructibleFiniteTor Λ X)
    (hG : ∀ C : ConstantModelConstructibleFiniteTor Λ X,
      ∃ i : G, Nonempty (C.obj ≅ (g i).obj))
    (hG_skeletal : ∀ i j : G, Nonempty ((g i).obj ≅ (g j).obj) → i = j) :
    ∃ hSums : HasCoproducts.{u + 1} (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory,
      letI := hSums
      ∀ (hL : ∀ i, localizingClosureProEtale Λ X (g i).obj) (i : G),
        IsCompactObject (⟨(g i).obj, hL i⟩ :
          (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory)
